1975 Councilors Breadon, Louijeune, Santana, Coletta Zapata, Culpepper, Durkan, Mejia, Pepén, Weber and Worrell offered the following: Resolution declaring Election Day a holiday for City Council employees and calling upon the City of Boston and the Commonwealth of Massachusetts to follow.
Councilor Coletta Zapata in the chair.
On motion of Councilor Breadon, Rule 12 was invoked to include Councilors Louijeune and Santana as original co sponsors.
On motion of Councilors Breadon, Louijeune, and Santana, the rules were suspended; the resolution was adopted: yeas 10 (Breadon, Coletta Zapata, Culpepper, Durkan, Louijeune, Mejia, Pepén, Santana, Weber, Worrell), nays 3 (FitzGerald, Flynn, Murphy).

Councilor Culpepper, on behalf of the Committee on Civil Rights, Racial Equity, and Immigrant Advancement, submitted the following:

1774 On the message and order, referred on September 23, 2026, Docket #1774, authorizing the City of Boston to accept and expend the amount of Five Hundred Thousand Dollars ($500,000.00) in the form of a grant, MOIA Mayors Migration Council, awarded by Rockefeller Philanthropy Advisors to be administered by the Department of Immigrant Advancement. The grant would fund support for city led programs that advance relief, inclusion, and opportunity for underserved communities in Boston through the Global Cities Fund, the committee submitted a report recommending that the order ought to pass.
The report was accepted; the order was passed: yeas 13 (Breadon, Coletta Zapata, Culpepper, Durkan, FitzGerald, Flynn, Louijeune, Mejia, Murphy, Pepén, Santana, Weber, Worrell).
